source_text: Quis autem iste est, qui uentis et mari imperat? (nimirum nouus - dominator atque possessor elementorum subacti iam et exclusi creatoris.' non ita est. sed agnorant substantiae auctorem suum, quae famulis quoque eius obaudire consuei uerant. inspice Exodum, Marcion aspice mari rubro, uastiorsuper omnia stagna Iudaeae, uirgam Moysi imperantem, ut funditus proscissum et pari utrimque stupore discriminis fixum sicco populum pede intestino itinere transmitteret, rursusque sub eiusdem uirgae nutu redeunte natura Aegyptium exercitum undarum concordia obrueret, in quod opus et austri seruierunt. lege et t sorte familiae dirimendae in transitu eius Iordanis machaeram fuisse, cuius impetum atque decursum plane et Iesus docuerat prophetis transmeantibus stare. (quid ad haec'? si tuus Christus est, non erit potentior famulis creatoris. sed his solis exemplis usus essem, si non etiam praedicatio marinae istius expeditionis Christum antecessisset nam cum transfretat, psalmus expungitur:
pass_a_gloss: For who is this one, who commands the winds and the sea? (certainly a new ruler and possessor of the elements, now subjected and excluded creator). It is not so. But they recognized the author of their substance, which was also accustomed to obey his servants. Look at Exodus, Marcion, look at the Red Sea, look at all the waters of Judea, the rod of Moses commanding, so that with the people cut off and fixed with equal wonder of judgment on dry foot on the internal journey, and again with nature returning at the nod of the same rod, the Egyptian army was overwhelmed by the harmony of the waves, in which work even the south winds served. Read also that in the division of his family at the crossing of the Jordan, a sword was present, whose onset and course Jesus had also taught the prophets to stand still while crossing. What is this? If your Christ is, he will not be more powerful than the servants of the creator. But I would have used only these examples, if also the preaching of this maritime expedition of Christ had not preceded, for when he crosses, a psalm is sung:

pass_b_english: So, who is this guy who's bossing the winds and the sea around? Apparently, he's some new big shot, ruler and owner of the elements, now that the actual creator has been subjected and excluded. Not quite. But what's going on here is that they're recognizing the author of their existence, the one whose servants they're also used to obeying. Take a look at Exodus, Marcion - check out the Red Sea, and all the other bodies of water in Judea, where Moses' rod was calling the shots, so that the people could cross on dry land, stuck in a state of utter astonishment, and then, with the rod's power still in effect, the Egyptian army got overwhelmed by the waves working together, with even the southern winds pitching in. And don't forget to read about how, when they were dividing up the family lands at the Jordan crossing, a sword was involved, whose attack and path Jesus had taught the prophets to stand still against while they were crossing. What's the point of all this? If your Christ is who you say he is, he's not going to be more powerful than the creator's servants. But I wouldn't have had to rely on just these examples if the story of Christ's journey on the water hadn't already been preached, because when he crosses the water, a psalm is sung, (no specific scripture reference is mentioned in the source).

review.notes: Pass A and Pass B both fail on the translation of 'agnorant'. The Latin 'agnorant substantiae auctorem suum' means 'they do not recognize/acknowledge their author of substance', whereas Pass A translates it as 'they recognized the author of their substance' and Pass B as 'they're recognizing the author of their existence'. This reverses the negation of the verb 'agnorant' (from agnosco, to recognize; agnosco/agnosco/agnorant is the negative form). Additionally, Pass B's translation of 'familiae dirimendae' as 'dividing up the family lands' is an interpretive addition not present in the text, which refers to the division of the people/families during the crossing.
reasons: Pass A and Pass B fail to preserve the negation of 'agnorant substantiae auctorem suum' (they do not recognize their author of substance). Pass A: 'they recognized the author of their substance'; Pass B: 'they're recognizing the author of their existence'.
